newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin court jails Bosnian for plane hijack.
newsitem.headline: Berlin court jails Bosnian for plane hijack.

text.p: A German court on Friday sentenced a Bosnian refugee to seven years in prison for hijacking an Austrian Airlines plane in January en route from Berlin to Vienna.

Salko Loncaric, a 40-year-old Bosnian roofer who had been living in Germany, had confessed at the opening of the trial, saying he had aimed to secure a German residency permit. His visa at the time was set to expire the following week.

The court ordered Loncaric to begin serving his sentence in a psychiatric clinic. He had admitted that he had been emotionally disturbed and under the influence of alcohol when he stormed the plane's cockpit.

Loncaric forced the pilot at knifepoint to return to Berlin. The January 7 incident ended without violence when police entered the plane from the rear and pushed Loncaric out of an open door on to the tarmac at Berlin's Tegel airport.
Loncaric told the court he had concealed a kitchen knife in his jacket, a 45-cm (18-inch) long wooden baton in his waistband and another bat in his carry-on luggage.
The incident sparked accusations that the western Berlin airport, which employs a private security company, was cutting costs at the expense of passenger safety.
The airport, which was known for its stringent security during the Cold War, denied the accusations.
The plane, a McDonnell-Douglas MD-80, was only one-quarter full with 28 passengers and five crew members. The passengers included Germans, Austrians and Japanese.
State prosecutors had pressed for a nine-year sentence, while Loncaric's defence argued for two years on probation.
